title: Trick Floor – Free Troll Platformer in a Jelly Castle
description: Play Trick Floor free in your browser: run and jump through 25 short levels where the floor drops, spikes pop out and the exit door runs away.
body: A cute jelly cube, a candy castle and 25 levels that lie to you. Floors drop away the moment you step on them, spikes pop out of nowhere, the ceiling falls, platforms turn out to be fake, gravity flips and the exit door gets up and runs away.

Every trap is hidden until it fires, and every death sends you straight back to the start of the level in half a second, so each try teaches you something. Levels are short, there is no text, and you earn up to three stars per level for dying as little as possible. It works with the keyboard or with big on-screen buttons on phones, tablets and Chromebooks, and your progress is saved.
New here? Read how to play and the tips to spot every trap.

title: How to Play Trick Floor – Controls, Traps and Stars
description: Trick Floor controls: arrows or A/D to run, Up, W or Space to jump; on touch, big left, right and jump buttons. Learn the traps and how stars work.
body: Goal: reach the castle door at the end of each level.
Keyboard: Left and Right arrows (or A and D) to run, Up, W, Z or Space to jump. Hold jump for a higher jump, tap it for a short hop.
Touch: two arrow buttons in the bottom left corner to run and a big yellow button in the bottom right corner to jump. You can slide your thumb between the arrows and press jump at the same time.

The traps: nothing looks dangerous at first. Some floor tiles drop a moment after you stand on them or as you get close, hidden spikes pop out of the floor or ceiling, ceiling blocks fall when you walk under them, a few blocks are fake and you fall through, darts shoot out of walls, invisible zones flip gravity so you walk on the ceiling, and the door itself may run away to somewhere else.
Dying is fine: you instantly restart at the beginning of the level with every trap reset, and the counter at the top goes up by one. There is no game over.

Stars: finish with few deaths for three stars (about one death per trap is allowed), a few more for two, and any finish gives one. Finishing a level unlocks the next one; the grid button opens the level select.

title: Trick Floor Tips: Beat Every Trap with Fewer Deaths
description: Practical tips for Trick Floor: how to deal with dropping floors, pop-up spikes, falling ceilings, fake blocks, darts, gravity flips and runaway doors.
body: Slow down near anything suspicious. Walking up to a trap at full speed is the most common way to die. Stop, take one step, and let it fire.
Falling ceilings can be baited. Step close enough to make the block drop, step back, then jump over it once it has landed.
Sinking floors give you a split second. If a tile starts to wobble under you, jump straight away. On sinking platforms over spikes, land and jump again in one motion.
Jump early over pop-up spikes. They come out when you get close, so take off a tile sooner than feels natural.
Doubt the odd platform. When two platforms offer two routes, one of them is often fake.
Darts fly along the floor. When a wall in front of you looks thick, be ready to hop.
Upside down, jump is still away from the floor you stand on. After a gravity flip, the ceiling is your floor and ceiling spikes are floor spikes.
The door runs, but not forever. Watch where it goes and follow it; the last spot is always reachable.
Stuck? On some portals you can watch an optional video to skip the level. You can always come back later for the stars.

title: Trick Floor FAQ
description: Answers about Trick Floor: is it free, does it save, does it work on mobile and Chromebook, how many levels, how stars work and how to skip a level.
body: Is it free? Yes, it is free to play in the browser, with no download and no sign-up.
How many levels are there? 25 short levels in five jelly colours. Most take between 5 and 30 seconds once you know the tricks.
Does it save my progress? Yes. Unlocked levels, stars and your fewest deaths per level are stored in your browser (or in your account on portals that offer it).
Does it work on phones and Chromebooks? Yes. On touch screens big left, right and jump buttons appear at the bottom; on computers use the arrow keys or WASD and Space.
Why did I die? I didn't touch anything! That is the joke. Every level hides one to five traps that only show themselves when they fire. Remember them and try again: you restart instantly.
How do stars work? Fewer deaths, more stars. Dying about once per trap still earns three stars.
Can I skip a level? On some game portals, after a few deaths a video button appears that skips to the next level. It is always optional.
Can I turn the music off? Yes, with the speaker button in the top right corner.

title: Trick Floor for Schools and Kids – Safe, Short, No Sign-up
description: Trick Floor is a short, text-free platformer that runs on school Chromebooks: no chat, no purchases, no account, levels of a few seconds each.
h1: Trick Floor for classrooms and kids
body: Trick Floor has no chat, no purchases, no account and no personal data. There is no text to read, only numbers and icons, so it works for any language and for early readers. Levels last a few seconds each and can be stopped at any moment.
It runs in the browser on Chromebooks, tablets and computers, with the keyboard or big on-screen buttons, and it is light (well under 1 MB plus music).

It is a gentle way to practise trial and error and resilience: every failure is instant, cartoonish and costs nothing, and the next attempt is always a little better. Ask students to predict where the trick is before they press play, or to describe a level's traps to a classmate in words.

Teachers can also use it for observation and memory (where did the trap appear?), planning (which route avoids it?) and counting (the death counter and the stars). The violence is mild cartoon slapstick: the jelly hero squishes and pops back.
Read how to play for the controls.
